builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: A Two-Level Clinical Novelty Prioritization Framework for Disease Trajectories Discovered from Longitudinal Electronic Health Records
summary: The method replaces clinician-adjudicated or purely structural ranking of discovered EHR disease-trajectory motifs with a two-level score combining embedding-based semantic sparsity against 166,972 PubMed references and reliability-adjusted clinical priority. It costs a one-time embedding and calibration pass over motif textualizations (feasible on a single GPU or CPU with bge-small-en-v1.5), but requires an upstream trajectory-discovery pipeline, MIMIC-IV-scale longitudinal EHR data, and a curated literature reference corpus. Hard top-k membership was unstable across encoders, templates, and score settings, the semantic score showed no monotonic forecasting benefit, and agreement with an independent RND baseline was low (q90 Jaccard = 0.125), so ranking decisions can shift under reasonable configuration changes.
rationale: The method addresses clinical-EHR research infrastructure and data prerequisites that fall outside a production AI/ML adoption decision, and its own robustness analyses show the prioritization is only stable at broad ordering granularity.
technique: Literature-relative novelty prioritization for EHR disease trajectories

claims.statement: The method replaces clinician-adjudicated or purely structural ranking of discovered EHR disease-trajectory motifs with a two-level score combining embedding-based semantic sparsity against 166,972 PubMed references and reliability-adjusted clinical priority. It costs a one-time embedding and calibration pass over motif textualizations (feasible on a single GPU or CPU with bge-small-en-v1.5), but requires an upstream trajectory-discovery pipeline, MIMIC-IV-scale longitudinal EHR data, and a curated literature reference corpus. Hard top-k membership was unstable across encoders, templates, and score settings, the semantic score showed no monotonic forecasting benefit, and agreement with an independent RND baseline was low (q90 Jaccard = 0.125), so ranking decisions can shift under reasonable configuration changes.

In the frozen catalog-q90 high-semantic subgroup, branch-enhanced forecasting reduced conditional event-time MAE by 20.1 days (95% CI, 13.3-27.0) and sMAPE by 2.37 percentage points (95% CI, 1.81-2.93); discrimination and endpoint-ranking differences were inconclusive.
